_comment: Mutation-coverage floors per crate, compared by .github/scripts/mutants-gate.py. The floor ratchets: a run may hold or improve it and may not fall below it. `target_caught_pct` is what docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md requires for release sign-off, and it is the destination rather than the floor — a gate that failed from day one would be switched off in a week. Record a new floor with `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-sync=1` locally, naming the crates and shard counts the run actually covered, or `mutants-gate.py <outcomes...> --update --expect-shards sunrise-domain=6,sunrise-core=4,sunrise-crypto=2,sunrise-sync=1` from a nightly's artifacts, in a commit that says what was added to earn it. The shard counts are not optional: `--update` banks whatever it is handed, so without them one shard of a crate becomes that crate's floor. Pass `--allow-partial` instead only when a floor covering just what ran is what you actually want. Every crate the run scores must appear here: the gate fails on a crate it measured and has no floor for, because a crate scored against nothing is a crate it is not protecting. `sunrise-core` is deliberately absent rather than seeded with a placeholder — a full pass over it is hours, so its floor is recorded from the first run that completes one, and until then the gate says so out loud. That rule named `sunrise-domain` too, and said both floors "are recorded from the first nightly run's artifacts". A complete local pass supersedes it, and this file now records `sunrise-domain`'s floor from one. The supersession is deliberate and the reason is the placeholder, not the nightly: the rule exists to stop a crate whose full pass is hours being seeded with a number nobody measured, and a complete 1356-mutant pass is not a placeholder wherever it ran. What it does not supersede is the `sunrise-core` half — that crate has no complete pass, local or nightly, so it stays absent, and #246 holds it. Every floor carries a `provenance` object — `sha`, `date`, `command` — and that, not this comment, is where each one's revision and invocation are recorded. `malformed()` in .github/scripts/mutants-gate.py requires it of any crate with a `caught_pct`, and `--update` writes it, so the next re-record cannot quietly drop it. The three fields have fixed meanings, because the field is only comparable across floors if they do: `sha` is the full 40-hex revision the mutants were MEASURED at, `date` is the day the measurement ran, and `command` is the invocation a person would type to reproduce it rather than the gate's own argv. `--update` does not ask git what HEAD is; it reads the revision from a revision.json written beside each outcomes.json while the measurement was running, by `mise run mutants` and by ci.yml's matrix, and it refuses when an outcomes file carries no stamp or when two stamps disagree. That gap is the reason: a sunrise-core pass is about five hours, the tests that motivated it get committed while it runs, and a floor stamped with HEAD at recording time names a revision that does not produce the number beside it. Floors recorded from now on also carry `dirty`, true when the measured tree had uncommitted changes. These three carry none, and absent means unknown rather than clean: they predate the stamp, and whether those working trees were clean is not something anyone can now establish, so writing `false` would be the invention the requirement exists to stop. What the fields cannot carry is why a revision was the right one to measure at, so that stays here: all three floors were taken locally and single-shard on 2026-09-16, but not at one revision. `sunrise-sync` is recorded against 164cc76, the commit that adds the three tests, rather than 1d4b484 with the other two, because 1d4b484 predates those tests and measures 36.89% on the same population, so recording sunrise-sync against it would name a revision that does not produce this number. One invocation per crate is what keeps each floor's revision its own: the task globs every outcomes file under out/mutants/ and hands the lot to the gate, and `--update` merges into this file per crate rather than replacing it, so the crates named in `--expect-shards` must be the crates whose results are on disk — a crate with outcomes and no expectation is a configuration error the gate refuses. Neither is a like-for-like improvement on its predecessor. `sunrise-crypto` went 78.43% -> 85.47% over a population that grew 296 -> 519 mutants as the crate did, and #96's six device-certificate width mutants -- the four field-width match guards and both `nickname.len() > 64` checks -- are confirmed caught in this run. `sunrise-sync` went 27.17% -> 48.36%, and most of that is not a test improvement at all: the old figure was measured without `--all-features`, which left all 94 of `src/sse.rs`'s mutants compiled out and therefore scored missed, so it described a build configuration. Same tree, feature on, before any test was added: 36.89%. See #193 and docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md §Features. The remaining 11.5 points are three tests added with it. `sunrise-sync`'s one timeout (`TokenSource::set` replaced with `()`) sits in the denominator and not the numerator, which is why the rate is 59/122 = 48.36% and not the 60/122 = 49.18% that scoring it as caught would give. 48.76% is 59/121, which is dropping the timeout from the denominator altogether — how the gate treats `unviable`, not how it would treat a caught mutant. `sunrise-domain`'s counterfactual below is computed by the caught rule, and this one now matches it. `sunrise-domain`'s floor is that first full pass, run locally at 1d4b484 on 2026-09-16 and recorded by its own `mise run mutants-baseline --expect-shards sunrise-domain=1`: 1356 mutants in 2h, single shard, nothing extrapolated. The counts reconcile against what the rest of the repository records independently: 1004 + 197 + 23 + 132 = 1356, the population .github/workflows/ci.yml's matrix comment and docs/10-cross-cutting/testing.md's cost table each carry on their own, and 1004 / (1356 - 132 unviable) = 1004/1224 = 82.03% by the gate's own rule. Its 23 timeouts are worth knowing before anyone reads the 82.03% as brittle. Every one of them is `+=` replaced with `-=` or `*=` on a cursor advance, so they are non-terminating mutants rather than a slow machine, and they will be 23 on any machine. This comment used to add that all 23 sit in a `parse` loop and split them 14 in capture.rs, 6 in sort_order.rs, 3 in annotate.rs. Both halves of that are withdrawn. `cargo mutants --list -p sunrise-domain --all-features`, re-run at e9a4c09, lists 1356 mutants — which reconciles with the counts above — and among them 4 `+=` mutants in sort_order.rs, not 6, in `between` and `above_tail`; `grep -n "fn parse" crates/sunrise-domain/src/sort_order.rs` returns nothing, so that file has no `parse` loop for a timeout to sit in. 6 timeouts cannot come out of a population of 4, so the split is wrong wherever the remaining 19 actually land. capture.rs carries 18 `+=` mutants, 12 of them in `parse` and the other 6 in `parse_duration_s` and `next_weekday`, so `parse` is where most but not all of them are. The honest limit: `--list` gives populations, and a timeout is a subset of a population, so listing refutes a per-file timeout count it is smaller than and can confirm none of them. Recovering the true split needs another full pass over the crate, which nobody has run since, so the per-file attribution is simply gone rather than restated from a number that was already wrong. The total is not in doubt: 23 is what the `timeout` field above records and what the 82.03% is computed from. They sit in the denominator and not the numerator: counting them as caught would read 83.90% and would mean an infinite loop had improved the score. What they do say is that the loops those cursor advances drive have no asserted progress guarantee, which is a real gap and a separate piece of work from recording this floor: it is filed as #245, and #245 is where moving this floor belongs. Recording the floor at all is not free, and the cost sits here beside it. The gate ratchets, so 82.03% is a standing constraint from now on — on a crate neither #96 nor #193 asked to constrain, enforced against six CI shards from a measurement taken on one. What bounds that is `.cargo/mutants.toml`'s `timeout_multiplier = 5.0` and `minimum_test_timeout = 120`, both relative to a per-invocation baseline, so a slower runner gets a proportionally longer mutant timeout rather than a spurious breach.
